title: Proper qcqs integral-to-rational scalar comparison with the counit normalization
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $F\subseteq E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure, $A=\mathcal O_F$, and $\Lambda=E$, with their induced norm topologies as in [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Let $h:U\to V$ be a proper morphism of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use $A_W=p_W^*\underline A$, $\Lambda_W=p_W^*\underline\Lambda$, the ordinary unbounded derived module-object categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and $T_W=\Lambda_W\otimes^L_{A_W}-$ in the universe [def-weil-size-convention]. For every $J\in\mathrm D_{\mathrm{ctf}}(U,A)$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible], the canonical coefficient-change map
$$\rho_{h,J}:T_V Rh_{*,A}J\longrightarrow Rh_{*,\Lambda}T_UJ$$
is an isomorphism. Its definition is the transpose under $h_\Lambda^*\dashv Rh_{*,\Lambda}$ of
$$h_\Lambda^*T_V Rh_{*,A}J\xrightarrow{\sim}T_U h_A^*Rh_{*,A}J\xrightarrow{T_U(\varepsilon_{h,A,J})}T_UJ,$$
where the first arrow is the inverse of the scalar/pullback mate of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization], transported by the canonical section-module equivalences [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport]. Thus this is the coefficient projection map with its specified counit. No geometric base-change assertion and no Noetherian, characteristic, dimension or invertibility-of-$\ell$ hypothesis is included. The coefficient field here is finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$; the analogous assertion for all continuous functions into the norm-topological algebraic closure is false in this general qcqs scope (see the statement dispute in the split report).

source.place: (2), scalar extension in the proper closed-complement calculation. Agent proper coefficient projection lemma for this qcqs finite-model scope. The full all-continuous norm-topological clause is not attributed to a finite-subextension-valued coefficient comparison or to the colimit-topological algebraic closure.

proof.text: Pass to section-ring modules using [lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization] and [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction]. These identify the ordinary unbounded derived functors, scalar extensions and the specified adjunctions, including their counits. Consequently proving invertibility of the section-ring counit mate proves invertibility of the internal map. By [pqf-lem-proper-basic], $h$ is qcqs. By the boundedness in [sk-def-sfb-constructible], $J$ is bounded below. No proper finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis has been inferred.

Factor the coefficient inclusion as $A\to F\to E$. Apply [lem-sfb-localized-direct-image-comparison] to $h$ and $J$, with its finite field named $F$. Its hypotheses are exactly qcqs and bounded below, verified in step 1. It gives an isomorphism $\gamma^1_J:F_V\otimes^L_{A_V}Rh_{*,A}J\to Rh_{*,F}(F_U\otimes^L_{A_U}J)$, and expressly defines this map as the counit transpose with the canonical pullback/tensor comparison. Put $K=F_U\otimes^L_{A_U}J$.

source.place: Lemma 5.3(1); the finite local-field localization is Lemma 5.6 and Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 6.8.2(2), using only the finite field case.

proof.text: Choose an $\mathcal O_F$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $\mathcal O_E$ using [lem-sfb-local-field-integral-basis]. Applied with the smaller field $F$ and larger field $E$, [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-finite-free] gives $F_W^{\oplus d}\cong E_W$ and says that the same basis works after $h^{-1}$. The tensor coordinates of [lem-sfb-finite-free-scalar-coordinates] therefore identify restriction of $E_W\otimes_{F_W}M$ with $M^{\oplus d}$, by $e\otimes m\mapsto(q_i(e)m)_i$, with inverse $(m_i)\mapsto\sum_i b_i\otimes m_i$. Apply these formulas termwise to complexes. Finite direct sums preserve exact sequences and quasi-isomorphisms, so the same coordinates compute the derived extension for every complex, including $K$. No boundedness of $Rh_*K$ is needed.

source.place: Finite integral basis, continuous coefficient coordinates and their inverse-image compatibility; the final termwise derivation is the elementary finite-sum argument.

proof.text: Let $\gamma^2_K:E_V\otimes^L_{F_V}Rh_{*,F}K\to Rh_{*,E}(E_U\otimes^L_{F_U}K)$ be the counit mate. Restrict it to $F_V$-modules. The direct-image/restriction isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] preserves its adjoint transpose. In the coordinates of step 3 its transpose on the $i$th summand is $\varepsilon_{h,F,K}$ followed by the $i$th inclusion into $K^{\oplus d}$: the basis vector $b_i$ pulls back to that same vector. Hence its $i$th component is $Rh_{*,F}$ of this inclusion, by the adjunction bijection. The additive functor $Rh_{*,F}$ preserves finite biproducts: applying it to $p_i\iota_j=\delta_{ij}$ and $\sum_i\iota_i p_i=1$ gives the inverse coordinate maps. Thus the restricted map is exactly the canonical isomorphism $(Rh_{*,F}K)^{\oplus d}\to Rh_{*,F}(K^{\oplus d})$. Scalar restriction reflects isomorphisms by the cited node, so $\gamma^2_K$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules); finite biproduct identities and the adjunction bijection give the displayed coordinate computation.

proof.text: Use K-flat representatives to identify the composite scalar extension with $T_W$: the isomorphism $E_W\otimes_{F_W}(F_W\otimes_{A_W}P)\cong E_W\otimes_{A_W}P$ sends $e\otimes f\otimes p$ to $ef\otimes p$, with inverse $e\otimes p\mapsto e\otimes1\otimes p$. Extension carries flat-term K-flat representatives to such representatives by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to the identity underlying topos and the coefficient ring maps. Thus these very formulas identify the derived functors. Paste $E_V\otimes^L_{F_V}\gamma^1_J$ with $\gamma^2_K$. Both are invertible. The pasting formula of [lem-sfb-pasted-mates-counit-normalization], with $b$ and $t$ identities, says its transpose is the composite of the two pullback/scalar comparisons followed by $T_U\varepsilon_{h,A,J}$. On the same representatives the comparisons of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] preserve $1\otimes p$; the preceding multiplication formula identifies their composite with the comparison for $A\to E$. Therefore this transpose is precisely the one defining $\rho_{h,J}$. Uniqueness of the adjunct proves that the invertible composite equals $\rho_{h,J}$.

source.place: Tags 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat) and 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition); categorical pasting is the explicit counit-normalization lemma cited in this step.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NB-01bd45493 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Not superseded: in live, clones/live and side-live the item is unsplit and unreviewed, there is no LAND line and no repair note; NC/ND/NE/NI/NJ deliveries of the same item are still in flight. The delivery drops the base clause Λ=Q̄_ℓ (all continuous functions, norm topology, per sk-def-localizing-closure) and keeps the finite-E case with the same ρ and counit normalization. This is a proper E7 correction, reported under '## Source error'. I checked the counterexample step by step and it holds. V=Spec C(N∪{∞},F̄_5); U⊂C_V has fibres D_n (n points) and C over ∞; h is proper, qcqs and not of finite presentation; J is the sign local system of an order-2 isogeny, so J∈Dctf. RΓ(C,L/3^r)=0, and proper base change plus repleteness give Rh_*J=M[0] with M(V) the null sequences. Γ(U,J_Ω) is the null sequences in Ω^n. Sections of the sheaf tensor Ω_V⊗M are locally finite sums, so at points over n their coordinates span at most N dimensions over F. The section w_n=3^n(α_{n,j}), with the α F-independent and integral, has span n, so H^0(ρ) is not surjective. This is unlike Q21 cdc69125, where the counterexample did not refute the statement. Steps: (1) the section-module transport nodes give the derived adjunctions with counits; pqf-lem-proper-basic gives qcqs; Dctf⊂Dbc gives bounded below. (2) lem-sfb-localized-direct-image-comparison applies to A=O_F→F: its only hypotheses are qcqs and bounded below, and its map is the counit adjunct. (3) The integral-basis, finite-free and coordinate nodes give E⊗_F−≅(−)^d, exact and computed termwise. (4) ring-sheaf-change-adjunction's comparisons b and d, with the adjunct compatibility, reduce the mate to the finite biproduct isomorphism; marking this elementary is fair. (5) The pasted-mates normalization, χ preserving 1⊗p, and K-flat pullback identify the composite with ρ. Edge cases F=E, J=0 and ramified E/F are fine. No new nodes, no duplicates; same_as=[] is consistent with my search (lem-sfb-continuous-algcl-proper-scalar-comparison is the finite-type-over-k Q̄ node). The off-unit nodes are generic coefficient and derived-category tools declared in split_report.tool_uses; I accept them. Batch-5: lem-pd-section-derived-pushpull-normalization is general internal↔section derived normalization, not a step of Poincaré duality or of the trace formula; lem-sfb-localized-direct-image-comparison is a generic A→E localization that reaches sec-poincare-duality only through that node. Both are accepted. MAINTAINER: the landed parent lem-sfb-qcqs-proper-constructible-closed-base-change steps 4 and 6 cite this item for C(−,Q̄_ℓ). That branch is now unsupported; the grandparent open-boundary-vanishing needs it. Reopen the parent, for example with a finite-type scope via lem-sfb-continuous-algcl-proper-scalar-comparison, and record this in HUMAN.md. No fixes.
